A partnership programme on institutional strengthening and capacity development for gender equality implemented by the Swedish Gender Equality Agency and the Agency for Gender Equality in BiH

The GEAR Up is a partnership programme on institutional strengthening and capacity development for gender equality implemented by the Swedish Gender Equality Agency and the Agency for Gender Equality in BiH. The program has two main goals 1. Institutional mechanisms for gender equality are strengthened and effectively implemented in line with gender equality commitments through effective structures and systems, across government and at all relevant levels. 2. Strengthened systems, mechanisms and instruments to achieve gender equality in all areas of society.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Overall, the programme made meaningful progress during 2025 despite a delayed start caused by the fact that the governmenttogovernment agreement between Sida and the Agency for Gender Equality of Bosnia and Herzegovina was not yet in place. Since the agreement was only signed in July 2026, preparatory work throughout 2025 was carried out through UN Women, while the Swedish Gender Equality Agency continued its technical engagement and planning on the Swedish side.
Although the absence of a formal agreement limited the ability of GEA BiH to implement several planned activities, the partners applied an adaptive approach that maintained cooperation, safeguarded momentum, and strengthened institutional relationships between the Swedish Gender Equality Agency, UN Women, and the BiH gender institutional mechanisms. During the reporting period (JanDec 2025), the programme contributed to improved institutional dialogue, increased awareness of gender mainstreaming methodologies, and a stronger understanding of monitoring systems and gender statistics within BiH institutions. These achievements represent essential prerequisites for the programmes longterm objectives once full implementation begins under the signed agreement. The study visit to Sweden in November 2025 was a particularly significant milestone. It provided GEA BiH and the two Gender Centres with firsthand exposure to Swedish gender equality governance and strengthened cooperation with the Swedish Gender Equality Agency. Engagement in regional and international policy discussions helped situate the programme within broader reform and governance frameworks and ensured continued visibility despite the transitional arrangements. Challenges remain, including limited institutional capacity, uneven political commitment, and insufficient genderdisaggregated data. These structural constraints will continue to influence the pace of implementation. Nevertheless, the programme demonstrated strong adaptive management and a clear ability to navigate institutional complexity during the bridging phase. A clear example of adaptive management during 2025 was the decision to redirect several planned capacitybuilding activities from GEA BiH to UN Women when it became evident that the governmenttogovernment agreement would not be signed within the expected timeframe. Instead of pausing implementation, the Swedish Gender Equality Agency worked with UN Women to adjust the sequencing of activities, enabling preparatory work to continue without interruption. For instance, technical workshops on gender mainstreaming and monitoring systems, which were originally intended for direct implementation with GEA BiH, were reorganised and delivered through UN Women, allowing BiH institutions to participate and benefit even before the formal agreement was in place. This ensured continuity, preserved institutional engagement, and prevented the programme from losing momentum during the bridging phase
